This device gives Mammon no way into shared storage that other apps can see too, so a mount there would be invisible to them. Use /mnt/nas for the root mount, or the NFS share (SAF) card to browse the share without root.
The share was mounted, but it never appeared in shared storage where other apps could see it, so Mammon removed it again: %1$s
The share was mounted, it never appeared in shared storage where other apps could see it, and Mammon could not remove it again — press Unmount to clear it: %1$s
No NFS server configured yet. Save host and export first.
The server did not answer in time.
Need a host and an export path like /export/data.
Enter an absolute mountpoint path starting with / (a bare "/" is not valid).

That path is Android\'s own storage plumbing: a physical SD card or USB volume under /storage has no shared-storage view to propagate a mount into, and /data/media sits below the daemon that serves shared storage, so a mount there reaches no app. Use shared storage itself, for example /storage/emulated/0/nfs, or a path of your own like /mnt/nas.
Type the folder that path really means: a mountpoint cannot contain a . or .. step. Use /storage/emulated/0/nfs, not /storage/emulated/0/../nfs.
Mount a folder inside shared storage, not the whole of it — try /storage/emulated/0/nfs.
Android owns the Android folder in shared storage — pick a different folder, for example /storage/emulated/0/nfs.
Enter the server host or IP.
Enter an export path starting with /.
Port must be 1–65535.
User ID must be a whole number from 0 to 4294967295.
Group ID must be a whole number from 0 to 4294967295.
Extra groups must be up to 16 comma-separated numbers from 0 to 4294967295.
Cannot reach the NFS server — is it up?
File exceeds the 64 MiB read limit of this provider.

This device cannot open share files for writing: its kernel does not provide the file bridge Android needs for it. Reading and creating files still work; for writes, try Filesystem mount (requires root).
